newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: THREDBO SURVIVOR'S RECOVERY AMAZES DOCTORS
Thredbo landslide survivor Stuart Diver is expected to be released from hospital this week.
Mr Diver has already been released from the intensive-care ward and was in a stable condition this morning.
Doctors have said they are amazed at his speedy recovery. His only remaining problem is the effect of frostbite on his toes.
Authorities have confirmed that nine people are dead and ten are still missing in the rubble.
Specially trained police teams have been locating and removing the bodies, and documenting the removal process on video.
Dental records will be used to identify those victims who have been found.

Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer has extended his hopes and sympathy to the families and friends of those still missing. Mr Fischer will spend most of the day in Thredbo, and will attend an ecumencial service with Governor-General Sir William Deane and Opposition Leader Kim Beazley.
He has congratulated rescue workers, but has expressed concern about some of the media coverage of the tragedy.
Mr Fischer said while the majority of the media had made a tremendous, professional effort, he thought the Press Council should have a look at the issue.
He said there were lessons to be learnt from the tragedy, and scope to examine ethical guidelines.
Meanwhile, Thredbo managers said they had received phone calls and letters of support from thousands of Australians.
Managing director David Osbourn said a relief fund had been set up for the families of victims, beginning with ten per cent of the resort's earnings for the rest of the season.
Donations can be mailed to the Thredbo Family Relief Fund at GPO Box 3600, Sydney, 2001.
HOPE REMAINS AS THREDBO PRAYS FOR LANDSLIDE VICTIMS
Thredbo locals still hope to find more survivors of the landslide, according to one of the church leaders preparing for today's ecumenical prayer and reflection service.
Father Wally Stefanski will join other church dignatories, Governor-General Sir William Deane, Acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer and Opposition Leader Kim Beazley at the service.
Father Stefanski said people were clinging to the hope that some of those trapped are still alive.
"The people now understand the whole process of healing," he said.
"They're still waiting for another miracle. We still have hope and trust in God."
Police at the landslide site said they were on track to remove most of the rubble by Thursday.
The process has moved more quickly since extra machinery was brought on to the site.
Mr Fischer said he would be taking a message of "absolute commendation" to the rescue teams when he visits Thredbo today.
He said wanted to extend hope and sympathy to the families and friends of those still missing, and congratulate rescue workers.
POLICE NAME OFFICIER SHOT DURING RAID
Police have released the name of a detective shot on duty in Brisbane last night.
He was Detective Sergeant Lenny Hooper from the Fortitude Valley CIB.
Detective Sergeant Hooper was shot in the chest during a raid on a unit in the inner-city suburb of Herston.
Police spokesman Brian Swift said Commissioner Jim O'Sullivan had spent the morning with the officer's widow and family.
"The Commissioner this morning got a personal phone call from the Governor, passing on his sympathies and understanding for the plight of the police at the moment," Mr Swift said.
NATIONAL PLEA TO MISSING PERSONS
People who have left their past lives behind are being asked to contact police to let them know they are all right.
The call has been made at the launch of Operation Safe and Well in an effort to end the uncertainty of the families of people who have gone missing.
A toll-free hotline will operate today as part of National Missing Persons Week.
New South Wales Police Commissioner Peter Ryan said people who call the hotline on 1 800 333 000 will not have to answer questions.

He said: "My message to any person who's chosen to walk away from their past and might have since been reported missing by their family and friends is: look, you haven't committed a crime, you're not in trouble with the law by going missing, all we want to know is that you're safe and well."
TWO AUSSIES QUALIFY FOR ATHLETICS CHAMPIONSHIP FINALS
Two Australians have qualified for finals at the world athletics championships in Athens.
Cathy Freeman qualiied tonight's final of the 400 metres after finishing second in her semi-final, behind American Jearl Miles-Clark.
Victoria's Darren Wilson qualified for the 10,000 metres final with a fifth placing in his heat.
Australia's Melinda Gainsford-Taylor failed to qualify for the final of the women's 100 metres which was won by American Marion Jones.

Another American, Maurice Greene, beat defending and Olympic champion Donovan Bailey in the men's 100 metres final. Australia's Margaret Crowley finished ninth in her heat of the 1500 metres, and failed to qualify for the semi-finals.
